headline: White House cuts data centers, batteries, and AR from US critical tech list, adds post-quantum crypto
summary: The US White House has updated its Critical and Emerging Technologies list, shrinking it from 18 to 14 categories. This first rewrite since 2024 removes data centers and AR/VR, while adding post-quantum cryptography and integrated photonics.
details: The White House Office of Science and Technology Policy has published its renewed National Security Science & Technology Strategy, rewriting the federal Critical and Emerging Technologies (CET) list. This is the first update since February 2024, reducing the list from 18 to 14 categories.

Significant cuts include advanced cloud services, high-performance data storage, data centers, batteries, grid integration, gas turbine engines, and augmented and virtual reality. These removals indicate a strategic shift in national priorities.

New additions to the CET list feature post-quantum cryptography, integrated photonics, high entropy alloys, and "hardened operating systems for consumer use." These technologies are now considered crucial for national security and future innovation.

Federal agencies utilize the CET list to guide export control rules, screen foreign investments via CFIUS, vet federally funded research proposals, and set R&D budget priorities. Therefore, these changes carry substantial weight across various sectors.

The removal of data centers is particularly notable, occurring amid the industry's largest buildout. This decision aligns with the strategy's guidance for agencies to complement, rather than compete with, private sector investment, as hyperscalers drive capacity.

The advanced computing category was renamed future computing technologies, losing advanced cloud services and data centers. It now includes edge computing for tactical environments, photonic and neuromorphic modalities, and advanced spatial computing.

The AI category also saw revisions; "AI safety, trust, security, and responsible use" and "AI assurance and assessment techniques" were replaced. The new focus is on "interpretability and control" and "adversarial robustness and AI security."

AI and autonomy expanded to absorb robotics and uncrewed systems, gaining multi-agent systems, swarm intelligence, autonomous agent identification, continual learning, and privacy-preserving machine learning. World systems are now a named class of foundation model.

Post-quantum cryptography appears for the first time, alongside operational technology and industrial control system security, and AI-enabled autonomous cyber capabilities. Integrated photonics is a new semiconductor subfield, and 2D materials are now explicitly named in novel materials.
